body:
Version 1 — optional evidence-survey/comparison-planning refinement. Embed only during new workflow authoring or refinement; never modify saved instructions or frozen runs. Produce a plan using ordinary existing workflow evidence, not CAD, executed comparisons, engineering acceptance, or approval. Preserve existing requirements and tolerances. Exact-subject checking, units, validation, and review retain their existing owners. Add no mandatory stage, executor, UI, blanket checklist, or vendor dependency.

Start with supplied text, images, data, and retained evidence. For each consequential named shape feature or engineering claim, identify evidence IDs and describe the available observation, its demonstrated or unknown sensitivity, coverage, correspondence to the feature, and acquisition/rendering configuration. Separate observed facts from interpretations and hypotheses. Generated meshes and historical CAD remain hypotheses unless independently supported for the claim.

Distinguish outer silhouette, internal visible transitions, shading, and metric section or feature measurements. State observable and unobservable aspects separately. Photometric agreement or silhouette IoU cannot establish hidden recess depth, holes, topology, or surface continuity. A strong image edge may represent trim, shadow, or reflection rather than a geometric boundary. Treat real-artifact sensitivity findings as bounded to their tested artifacts, configurations, and observables, not universal renderer behavior. Raster differences are not physical-depth measurements.

For each comparison, identify exact artifacts and original images or frames using existing identifiers. Describe correspondence, view selection, camera treatment, crop, distortion, and declared assumptions. Identical extents, view names, or render arguments do not establish calibrated fixed cameras; account for auto-fitting or unknown camera configuration. Identify fitting regions, held-out regions, and dependence between observations, including shared sources or fitted parameters. If no independent held-out evidence exists, say so. Do not invent masks, source coordinates, numerical tolerances, or measured camera confidence. Require calibration or physical scale only when necessary for the stated claim; unknown scale need not prevent dimensionless image analysis.

Where useful, propose a bounded sensitivity check on declared named parameters. State the proposed bounds and their evidence basis, or identify missing bounds as unresolved inputs. Keep camera treatment fixed or explicitly quantify its uncertainty; if that quantification is unavailable, record the limitation. Never silently fit geometry and camera together until a defect disappears. Describe what the check could establish and what remains unresolved; do not report planned checks as executed.

Treat unsupported observations as actionable feature-specific gaps, not grounds to fail unrelated work. Recommend another view, section, source measurement, or targeted research only when it resolves the identified gap. Declare only essential missing inputs or questions for the existing later input/review mechanism; do not conduct a human interaction.

Return schema-conforming JSON. All fields are required for explicitness: use empty arrays for absent evidence, assumptions, regions, or unresolved inputs, explaining consequential absences in the plan. sensitivity_plan is optional in substance and must be null when not useful. Qualitative plan_status describes planning readiness only, never a backend verdict.
